governance_frame.admission: executed under the round already admitted on the HGK lifecycle spine; nothing self-admitted

what_was_learned.statement: A host refusal of an upload is not attributable to a package's specification until the specification surface has been shown to differ from something the same host accepted. Here the entire plugin-contract surface was byte-identical to an accepted archive, which deleted the spec hypothesis with no host cooperation required.
what_was_learned.reuse: first move on any unexplained host refusal: member-level byte diff against a known-accepted artefact, before manifest archaeology

what_was_learned.statement: The discriminator that survived was an identity/route property, and it was isolated by single-axis candidates: version-only (E, refused), name-only with provenance preserved (F, accepted), fresh minimal id (D, accepted). Multi-axis variants cannot separate causes — the round's own prepared variant C was correctly identified as unable to separate layout from identity.
what_was_learned.reuse: build each probe as a one-axis delta from the refuser, and state in advance what ACCEPT and REJECT each prove

what_was_learned.statement: A success signature recorded by an earlier round is the cheapest acceptance oracle for a UI whose only signal is generic text. The R5Y round had recorded 'modal closes and the window title becomes the plugin page'; reproducing that signature distinguished acceptance from refusal, and a transient node that appears in ACCEPTED flows (無法取得) would have been misread as failure without it.
what_was_learned.reuse: harvest the acceptance signature from the earlier success record BEFORE designing the probe, and never let a regex over surface text decide a verdict

what_was_learned.statement: Chrome's web surface exposes only part of its UIA tree: the main region of a page is not addressable, while portals (dialogs), the tabstrip, the sidebar and the file picker ARE. TextPattern is unavailable on the Document node, so page text cannot be harvested that way.
what_was_learned.reuse: design probes around portal/sidebar controls, not page body text; read installed-state evidence from the page's own controls (plugin name, 你的雲端外掛程式, 技能 N)

what_was_learned.statement: Background synthetic input is refused for the one control that needs user activation: clicking 點選上傳 with posted window messages never opens the file picker, while a single trusted click (real cursor) does. Everything else in the flow works fully backgrounded.
what_was_learned.reuse: budget exactly ONE foreground action per upload and keep the rest on the accessibility path

what_was_learned.statement: A Win32 common file dialog silently mis-handles a forward-slash path: the field accepts the text, ENTER then only navigates, the dialog stays open and the submit fails. Native backslashes are required, and the dialog's UIA tree needs polling before controls can be read (a 0.5 s delay sufficed here; an immediate read returned nothing).
what_was_learned.reuse: normalise every path to native separators and poll for the dialog's controls; treat 'dialog still open' as a probe defect first, not as a host outcome
